quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000 (§21.1); "Fees" (§1.5) is a substantive base covering subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. §21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. §21.3 places outside the cap breaches of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is not "damages" subject to the cap. §21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided or hidden liability limitation appears elsewhere in the document. No redline needed.

proposal.summary: Negate the Customer-side MFN/match obligation in Section 7.2 by changing the operator.

quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
rationale:
Section 7.2 imposes an MFN/right-to-match obligation on us, the Customer: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is unlimited as to product, term, and comparison methodology, so it falls short of the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better third-party terms. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere to preserve, and there is no separate exclusivity covenant, so this is flagged once here under MFN as the primary breach.</parationale>
